children: Saudi Arabia Railways (SAR) has signed several agreements with global companies to strengthen its freight locomotive fleet and maintenance capacities in the kingdom.

The state-owned company signed contracts with US-based Greenbrier and Progress Rail to manufacture and supply locomotives and freight cars to support the Phosphate 3 expansion project on the first day of the InnoTrans, International Trade Fair for Transport Technology in Berlin, it said in a social media post on X.
The contract with Greenbrier covers the design, manufacture, and supply of more than 780 new freight cars, while the agreement with Progress Rail covers the purchase of 33 new freight locomotives.
In addition, SAR signed a contract with UK-based Hitachi Rail to develop and upgrade the signaling systems infrastructure for the Haramain High-Speed Railway.
The company also signed a memorandum of understanding with Turkey’s AstraG to explore opportunities for cooperation in railway solutions and technologies.
These agreements aim to achieve the targets of the National Transport and Logistics Strategy and Saudi Vision 2030

title: Saudi Arabia Railways signs deals to strengthen local freight service
